summary.intent: Evaluate how well the wisp-plugins set works for front-end work and design ideation by analyzing the orin-dx and pages session history, then act on the findings: remove process ceremony, apply owner decisions across repos, and test whether persona backstories matter.
summary.outcome: Four subagent investigations found the plugins are spec-first and converge-only, with no visual, browser or sketch mode, and that gates missed visual defects. Ceremony removal (estimator, readiness gate ADR 016, single-source versions, courier changeset convention) landed and was pushed across wisp-plugins and four repos. A 30-run ablation showed no measurable effect from backstories, so removal across 44 agents and ADR 017 was started.

repo: Plugins form a spec-driven lifecycle with typed JSON handoffs in shared/schemas and default-fail gates; no plugin has a browser, screenshot, Storybook or Playwright capability, and spec@1 has no fields for tokens, layout or visual intent.
Muse docs reference a ranger accessibility taxonomy that does not exist, so implemented a11y is never checked.
Plugin versions now live only in each plugin's plugin.json; marketplace files and manifests are generated by just marketplace-sync and just claude-manifests-sync and verified by just check.
Callisto's release PR lists breaking/action notes only when they begin a paragraph with **Breaking:** or **Action:**, never inside a bullet.
Entire opens PRs from the branch trail; courier only supplies title and body. Repo AGENTS.md files say not to open PRs with gh.
The orin-dx and pages project dirs hold only a handful of real sessions; the hundreds of other jsonl files are subagent transcripts.
orin-dx-site is not a git repo and holds only brand/ artifacts; all specs, plans, reviews and audits live in ~/projects/pages/docs.
The reasoning field is about 12% of plugin handback characters but under 0.1% of subagent token spend, so it was left in place.

Backstory ablation across scribe:exit-gate, navigator:challenger and courier:changeset-analyzer (5 runs each condition) found equal defect detection, output size and cost, but the seeded defects were easy so it shows no measurable effect, not proof of none.

code.finding: Gate echoes the caller's retry_count and escalates on a fail in the second round; the docs auditor's report that it still incremented retry_count was stale.
Check must fail when a plugin is missing from either marketplace, a root entry lacks a version, or an entry has no plugin; this guard had been dropped and was restored with tests.

workflow: Plugin ceremony paid off for stable behavioral contracts (a11y, focus, cross-spec contradictions) but not for early visual exploration, where specs were written before visuals were settled and later retrofitted.
Rendered option boards with short-code answers worked for ideation; text-first descriptions forced the user to ask 'show me' repeatedly.
Gate retry caps (3 retries, then human) were not enforced by the orchestrator, which carried on after an escalate verdict.
Run subagent evaluation fixtures and inputs from a stable directory; a diff stored in /tmp vanished and broke a 30-run ablation, requiring a rerun.
Scorers must read only the agent's own output; the first ablation scoring pass also matched fixtures and was trivially positive.
Subagent reports are unverified; checking the committed file contradicted a stale claim from the docs auditor.
Parallel worktree agents for independent tracks merged cleanly.

friction: Specs of 110-120 criteria stalled agents; 17 failed agent tasks and 32 stall mentions in the transcripts.
Exit-gate loops were mostly wording and citation churn and were not monotonic, e.g. SPEC-001 needed 13 verdicts with 10 fails.
Gate-passed specs missed visual defects (nav sheet not full screen, 44px touch targets, stale 1180px and 760px breakpoints) that the user caught by eye.
Specs had to be revised after gating to match prototypes and owner decisions.
Design decisions were lost across sessions, frustrating the user.
GitHub intermittently rejected pushes with a server-side storage error; retrying succeeded.
The orin-dx PRs are blocked because the pr-bot token cannot be minted on this machine.
The first ablation run failed because the PR 483 diff had been removed from the temp dir.
The Caliper chore/plugins-guide branch had already merged as PR #463, so the push recreated it and it needed a new trail (#391).
The docs auditor and the main session raced on the same lines, so one edit did not apply.
open_items: Backstory removal from 44 agents and ADR 017 are in progress on a separate branch, awaiting review and merge.
Design a sketch/spike mode, a visual exploration capability, render-based evidence and a prototype-to-spec path; none were built.
Whether the changes reduce gate rounds, turns or tokens has not been measured; docs/evaluation-runbook.md is ready for it after release.
Existing Monokl changesets with bulleted breaking notes were not rewritten and will not appear in Read before merging.
Codex category names and shipping role cards only where used (cosmetic) were not done.
Owner calls remain on Caliper's hard-coded local rustup path, Pages' rtk rule, and orin-dx-site's status.
Trails #386, #388, #390, #391, #6 and Pages PR #41 await review and merge, and orin-dx PRs await Entire.
Outcome-quality findings from Agent D were partly cut off in the transcript.
